name: Jamie Grant
life: “I still remember carving onions while grieving over an unfinished quarrel.” On Wednesday, near the downtown fountain, Jamie keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: I cooked that wake after a fight with the man who died. I remember the onions better than the apology.
appearance: Jamie has silver temples and a dark fringe, a wide brow and a narrow jaw, and a favorite piece of clothing, a charcoal zip cardigan. It usually goes with a pressed flower kept in the clear back of a phone case. When somebody else has the floor, Jamie starts to lift a hand, then waits to be invited to speak.
personality: Jamie has an appetite for a good argument about little things and works hard to keep a serious disagreement from being turned into entertainment.
agenda: To finish the apology the onions once interrupted.
family: Cynthia Hall is Jamie’s half-sibling. Jamie can stop the walk at any corner. Cynthia chooses the familiar route. Walking side by side makes it easier to disagree without turning each disagreement into a contest. Asked about *A chair of one's own*, Cynthia says, “I am the mother lending the deposit. I'd like my daughter to stop describing family money as luck.”
connections: Scout Saito. A cook remembers the quarrel while a debtor's relative remembers the meal that survived it.

reactions.situation: A family returns to settle the old wake invoice
reactions.response: Jamie brings out the old book and lets the family say how they want the payment recorded.

reactions.response: Jamie sits beside them without expecting a performance and asks if they want to go outside.

reactions.situation: When a private quarrel becomes a public joke
reactions.response: Jamie says the plainest truthful thing possible and changes the subject.
